explanation: This pole fires when the token at the current position is only a cut-off piece of a larger unit: (i) a byte fragment of a multi-byte character that the tokenizer split (the leading or continuation byte(s) of a Greek/CJK/Hangul character, e.g. 'χωριο' -> ' �'+'�' fires 9.8, 'άνθρωποι' -> ' �'+'�' fires 5.1, while the whole characters that follow the split, 'ρ','ή','σ','τ', fall to 0-0.6), and (ii) a bare sub-word onset fragment that is not itself a word, chiefly the 'ch' onset in every spacing/case form (' ch', ' Ch', 'Ch', 'ch', '-ch', '_ch', '/ch', '(ch', '\tch') and the near neighbours 'gr', 'chr', 'Ches', 'grat', 'gro', plus lone non-Latin letters (' ч', ' خ', ' Х', ' k'). Strength grows with how much of the unit is missing (a lone lead byte reaches 32-45, a bare two-letter onset 5.5-12), and complete tokens are silent ('church' 0.00, 'chair' 1.06, 'cheated' 0.04, 'China' 0.02, and ' chanted' 12.14 next to ' church' 0.00 in one sentence); other onset fragments (' sh', ' sp', ' fl', 'pr', 'cl', 'th' at 0-0.9) do not fire, and complete proper names/role titles are a weaker, context-dependent second trigger (' Cristiano' 10.9, 'Chancellor' 8.0 after 'The report said' but 0.1-2.9 after 'In the garden,').
